newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia's Sihanouk pessimistic on crisis talks.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia's Sihanouk pessimistic on crisis talks.

text.p: Cambodia's King Norodom Sihanouk said on Monday he doubted foreign envoys would succeed in negotiating an end to Cambodia's crisis after Second Prime Minister Hun Sen rejected mediation.

The king, who is in Beijing for medical treatment, said he was willing to meet envoys from France, Japan, the United States and the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) who were due in Beijing this week.
But he said in an interview issued in his information bulletin that "The Strongman" -- meaning Hun Sen -- had not authorised them to intervene in Cambodia's internal affairs.
A copy of the interview was released by the palace in Phnom Penh on Monday.
"Hun Sen has already clearly rejected my proposals of mediation or political assistance in solving the actual problem," the king said.
Sihanouk called on his son, First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh, and Hun Sen to travel to Beijing for mediation talks after their supporters began fighting in the capital on July 5.
The next day, as Hun Sen's forces were pushing Ranariddh's men out of Phnom Penh, Hun Sen announced Ranariddh's ouster and said there was no need for mediation talks.
The king indicated on Sunday that he would not endorse Cambodia's new government, but stopped short of accusing Hun Sen of staging a coup.
He called on Hun Sen to respect the constitution and all laws and international agreements signed by the government since the 1991 peace treaty.

In a statement released on Sunday -- his first public statement since Ranariddh's ouster -- Sihanouk had said he was not willing to sign royal decrees and other documents covering the make-up of Hun Sen's "victorious" government.

Sihanouk also said he fully supported a United Nations Security Council resolution condemning the fighting between troops loyal to the two premiers and urging all parties to solve their differences peacefully.
Sihanouk himself was ousted as head of state in a republican coup in 1970. He was restored as monarch in 1993 after U.N.-organised elections.
The elections were narrowly won by Ranariddh's royalist FUNCINPEC party but the king negotiated a power-sharing agreement with Hun Sen.
